header: THE ALL-INDIA CONSUMER PRICE INDEX (CPI) AND THE INFLATION RATE, from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI): the monthly index of all India (Combined, Urban, Rural) and of each State and Union Territory, and the year-on-year inflation rate for the last 1, 3, 5 and 10 years. This is the CPI of the people at large; it is NOT the CPI for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW) of the Labour Bureau, on which the dearness allowance rests (src/lib/live/aicpi.ts). SOURCE: the open data service of MoSPI (api.mospi.gov.in, "eSankhyiki"), which I read without a login (a call is then limited to pages of 100 rows, which is all I need):
* from January 2026 the NEW series, base 2024 = 100: /api/cpi/getCPIData?base_year=2024&division_code=0 (the "CPI (General)" rows; year, month_code, limit, page)
* to December 2025 the OLD series, base 2012 = 100: /api/cpi/getCPIIndex?base_year=2012&series=Current&state_code=99&group_code=0 (the "General" rows of all India)

I read MoSPI's own inflation rate as it is given and do not work it out here: for the new series it is the rate over the same month of the year before, from the series linked back. So the chart of the rate is the old series to December 2025 and the new one after it, the way MoSPI and the sites that follow it (Trading Economics) draw it. Checked on 14 Nov 2026 against the figures of the Trading Economics chart: October 2026 6.09, January 2026 2.74, December 2025 1.33, October 2025 0.25; and against MoSPI's own dashboard: all-India Rural 110.73, Urban 109.22, Combined 110.05 for October 2026. A month MoSPI has not yet published is simply absent: I estimate nothing. MoSPI releases the index of a month on the 12th of the next (at 4 pm).

symbols.name: MONTHS_SHOWN
doc: The most months the column charts show at once (the latest twelve of the new series).

members.name: base
doc: "2012" (to December 2025) or "2024" (from January 2026).

members.name: month
doc: YYYY-MM

members.name: inflation
doc: MoSPI's inflation rate (percent, year on year).

symbols.name: monthsBetween
symbols.sig: export function monthsBetween(from: string, to: string): string[]
doc: The months from `from` to `to`, both included (YYYY-MM), oldest first.

symbols.name: latestDue
symbols.sig: export function latestDue(now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): string
doc: The latest month whose index MoSPI has published by `now`. The index of a month comes out on the 12th of the next, at 4 pm Indian time, and I count on that.

symbols.name: dueDay
doc: The day the index of `month` is due: the 12th of the month after it.

symbols.name: parseRows
symbols.sig: export function parseRows(json: unknown, base: "2012" | "2024"): CpiRow[]
doc: The rows of one reply, CHECKED: I keep only the "CPI (General)" rows (the new series) or the "General-Overall" rows (the old), each with a known month, State name, sector and a plausible index (60 to 400) and rate (-30 to 60 percent). A reply that is not the service's, or holds none of these rows, is an error: I never take an empty answer for truth.

symbols.name: paged
symbols.sig: async function paged(url: string, base: "2012" | "2024", get: JsonGetter): Promise<CpiRow[]>
doc: Reads every page of a query (100 rows a page, the most the service gives); I refuse a reply that says it has more than 40 pages.

symbols.name: askNew
symbols.sig: export async function askNew(year: number, months: number[], get: JsonGetter = defaultGetter): Promise<CpiRow[]>
doc: Asks for the new series (base 2024), every State, all three sectors, for these months of one year (month numbers 1 to 12).

symbols.name: askOld
symbols.sig: export async function askOld(years: number[], get: JsonGetter = defaultGetter): Promise<CpiRow[]>
doc: Asks for the old series (base 2012), all India, all three sectors, for these years: the inflation of the years before 2026.

symbols.name: askNewMonths
symbols.sig: export async function askNewMonths(from: string, to: string, get: JsonGetter = defaultGetter): Promise<CpiRow[]>
doc: Asks for the new months from `from` to `to` (YYYY-MM): one request per year.

symbols.name: askAll
symbols.sig: export async function askAll(now: DateTime = DateTime.now(), get: JsonGetter = defaultGetter): Promise<CpiRow[]>
doc: Asks for everything, for an empty store: the new series from January 2026 to the latest due month, and the old series from 2016 to 2025.

symbols.name: SectorSeries
doc: One sector's months, aligned to the month list of the answer. A month MoSPI has no figure for is null.

members.name: month
doc: YYYY-MM

members.name: value
doc: Percent, year on year (all India, Combined).

members.name: latest
doc: The latest month published, YYYY-MM.

members.name: months
doc: The months of the column charts (at most twelve, ending with the latest), oldest first.

members.name: states
doc: Each State and Union Territory, by name.

members.name: inflation
doc: All India Combined inflation, month by month, from January 2016.

members.name: next
doc: The month after the latest, and the day its index is due.

symbols.name: buildCpi
doc: Builds the answer from the saved rows. I add nothing and a missing month is null; a store without the new series (not yet loaded) is an error.

symbols.name: InflationSlot
doc: One month of the inflation chart: the rate, or null for a month for which MoSPI's service has no figure. I leave it blank on the chart and never fill it in.

symbols.name: inflationWindow
symbols.sig: export function inflationWindow(points: InflationPoint[], years: 1 | 3 | 5 | 10): InflationSlot[]
doc: The window of the inflation chart: the last `years` years, from the same month `years` years before the latest month to the latest (13 months for one year: October to October). It holds every month in it, and a month without a figure is null.

symbols.name: RBI_TARGET
doc: The Reserve Bank of India's inflation target (4%) and the tolerance band round it (2% to 6%).

members.name: level
doc: Above the upper limit (the alarm), within the band, or below the lower limit.

members.name: lead
doc: The few words in bold: "Inflation is above the RBI's limit."

members.name: text
doc: The sentence: the latest rate, how it moved since the month before, and where it stands against the band.

symbols.name: inflationAlert
symbols.sig: export function inflationAlert(points: InflationPoint[]): InflationAlert | null
doc: THE STATEMENT UNDER THE INFLATION CHART, which I write from the saved figures (so it is always about the latest month and never out of date): the latest rate, whether it rose or eased from the month before, and where it stands against the Reserve Bank's band. Above the upper limit it is the alarm, and says for how long ("for the first time since Oct 2024", or "for the 3rd month in a row"). What the market had expected is not in MoSPI's data, so I do not say it.

behaviours: the new series reads: 3 States x 3 sectors x 10 months
the old series reads: all India Combined, 120 months
the figures are MoSPI's own (all India October 2026: Combined 110.05 (6.09%), Urban 109.22, Rural 110.73)
a reply that is not an answer, or that has no General rows, is an error
a row with an implausible index or rate, an unknown sector or month is dropped
the old series' rows carry the base under the other spelling (baseyear) and are read
the latest month and the months of the chart (Jan to Oct 2026)
all India is the headline, the States are the others, in order, and All India is not one of them
West Bengal Urban follows MoSPI month by month (Jan 103.93 ... Oct 108.33)
the all-India tabs hold the three sectors
the inflation series joins the old and the new: December 2025 1.33 (base 2012) then January 2026 2.74 (base 2024)
the inflation series is in order from January 2016 to October 2026, and the two months MoSPI has no figure for (April and May 2020) are absent, not made up
the next month and the day its index is due
nothing saved of the new series is an error (never an empty chart taken for the truth)
a month that is missing for a State is null, not a made-up figure
only the latest twelve months are charted when more are saved
the 1-year window runs from the same month a year back (Oct 2025 to Oct 2026: 13 points, 0.25 to 6.09)
the 3, 5 and 10-year windows hold 37, 61 and 121 months
10 years begin in Oct 2016, and a month without a figure stays in the window as a gap (null)
a shorter record gives what it has

the alarm for October 2026: 6.09% from 5.54%, above the Reserve Bank's upper limit of 6% for the first time since October 2024 (read from the data: Oct 2024 was 6.21%, and every month since was below 6)
above for several months in a row: says how many and since when
exactly 6% is within the band, not above it; the band is 2% to 6% with a 4% target
below 2% is said to be below the lower limit; the very first month of a record, and a missing month before, still read
above for the first time in the whole record says so, and January looks back to December
months between two months, both included
MoSPI releases the 12th at 4 pm: before it the month before last is the latest due, after it the last month
the day the index of a month is due
every page is asked (100 rows a page, up to the pages the reply names) with the filters
months are asked a year at a time
the old series is asked for the years, all India, General
everything: the new months of 2026 to the latest due (October), and the ten old years
a reply that claims more than 40 pages is refused
a failing service is an error, not an empty answer
